name: Gaius
overview: Gaius is a male believer identified as being from Derbe, as noted in Acts 20:4. Beyond this geographic and faith-based detail, Scripture does not provide additional personal or tribal information about him. His mention highlights his role within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Gaius appears once in the biblical record in Acts 20:4. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to this name in the text, so it is presented plainly as a common proper name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Gaius beyond his identification as a believer from Derbe. There are no documented connections to other individuals or familial ties in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gaius's significance lies in his inclusion among the early Christians associated with the missionary efforts described in Acts. His presence from Derbe indicates the spread of the gospel beyond major urban centers, reflecting the growth of the church in diverse regions. Though details are sparse, his mention underscores the faithful individuals who supported the apostolic mission.
